attribution.note: Marcus states the tally in his own voice as fact. It closely follows the legislators' open letter he cites just before, but he asserts it without quotation marks or distancing, so he endorses it.

semantics.note: The proposition is verbatim and keeps 'or resolutions', the territories and 'at least 27 states'. This is a historical tally about 2024.

contract.note: The plain reading as a reported legislative tally is ordinary and fair. It counts states, not individual laws, and covers deepfake laws broadly, as the words allow.

evidence.note: This is a contemporaneous tally by state legislators dated December 2024, which the contract accepts as a source. It gives both counts and lists 30 states with deepfake laws, which is consistent with 'at least 27'. It is not Marcus's own writing. The underlying bills were not recounted.

reviews.rationale: A legislators' tally of the kind the contract accepts reports 31 states plus Puerto Rico and the Virgin Islands, and at least 27 states with deepfake laws, in 2024. This matches the claim. One caveat: the tally is dated December 12 and the bills were not independently recounted. The packet contains no counter-tally.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: 'Will be minimal, and short-lasting' is firm, so this is a scored forecast. Reading it as a national (US-China) advantage fits the context. The earlier 'if current trends continue' proviso arguably frames the whole paragraph; the contract flags this, and it does not change the result.

contract.note: The contract supplies no magnitude, duration or deadline and invents none. Its capability-based reading is fair. Early resolution is allowed only for a contradiction, which is reasonable for an unrestricted forecast.

evidence.note: Stanford AI Index 2026: the US-China gap has effectively closed, with the lead changing hands several times and a 2.7% US lead in March 2026. This fits the trend but cannot settle an open-ended future claim. It covers Arena performance only.

reviews.rationale: The forecast has no deadline, and no dated event meets the early-contradiction rule. The evidence shows US-China capability convergence with small, shifting leads. That is consistent with the forecast, but under the contract finite convergence cannot conclusively support an unrestricted future claim, so it stays unresolved.

attribution.note: Marcus's own parenthetical assertion in his own post.

semantics.note: This is a faithful rendering of the parenthetical as a present-tense observation about generative AI's profitability and speculative status.

contract.note: The contract chooses the period (2024), the aggregate industry scope and net income as the measure; the speaker supplied none of these. 'Still hasn't' could mean cumulative profit to date. The reading is reasonable, but the result depends on it, and an unknown accounting basis blocks a money score.

evidence.note: This reports a 2024 net loss of about $5bn at OpenAI, from audited statements. It covers one company only, not the industry aggregate. It was published before the evaluation date.
This is a 2023 secondary report that Midjourney was profitable. It covers one company, a different period, and an undefined profit measure, so it does not establish the aggregate.

reviews.rationale: The packet has no industry-wide net-income figure. OpenAI's 2024 loss and Midjourney's reported profitability are company-specific context. The accounting basis is unknown, which the contract says prevents a money score, and 'speculative' has no measure. The available evidence does not settle the aggregate claim.
